ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Geoscience
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Nature Geoscience is a monthly journal dedicated to publishing high-quality original research papers across all areas of the geosciences. The journal’s content reflects all the disciplines within the geosciences, including studies of the Earth’s climate system, the solid Earth and the planets. Nature Geoscience covers studies based on all the methods used by geoscientists, ranging from field work and numerical modelling on regional and global scales to theoretical studies and remote sensing. Physical, chemical and biological investigations that contribute to our understanding of the Earth system or the planets are all represented.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Sea level-induced oyster reef accretion causes minimal net carbon burial change
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Geoscience, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02121-y

Oyster reefs in North Carolina have grown vertically as sea level has risen in recent centuries, although this has not led to an increase in carbon sequestration, according to an analysis of oyster reef cores.
ns1:item.dc:title: Sea level-induced oyster reef accretion causes minimal net carbon burial change

ns1:item.ns1:title: Transient variability in global oceanic oxygen during the Last Interglacial Period
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Geoscience, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02120-z

Global marine oxygen levels probably peaked after the start of the Last Interglacial before declining, reflecting the influence of shifts in Southern Ocean temperature and sea-ice extent, based on a global reconstruction using a thallium isotope redox proxy.
ns1:item.dc:title: Transient variability in global oceanic oxygen during the Last Interglacial Period
